description:
FILED s506f (Opus, s507 resume, 2026-10-04) from the companion mover io/nargv.t (C 11/2 -> 5/1).

The mover is NOT a regression of the switch work: on main `local $^I = '.bak'` bound a DOWN-cased symbol
(the bare `$^I` token under :invert -- the same bug as F1's `local $^W`), so the in-place edit was never in
effect and nargv.t's rows "passed" by printing to STDOUT.  s506f's F1 fix (`_transform_pkg_var` pipe-quotes a
caret variable) makes `local $^I` real, and the file's NESTED in-place edit is then wrong.

MINIMAL PROBE (scratch/s506f/s507/nargv-min.sh in worktree agent-a908d9d2d9fff4ce2):
    { local *ARGV; local $^I = '.bak'; @ARGV = qw(a b);
      while (<>) { other() if $. == 2; print "X$_"; } }
    sub other { local *ARGV; local *ARGVOUT; local $_; @ARGV = qw(c);
      while (<>) { print "Y$_" } }
    a = "a1\na2\n", b = "b1\n", c = "c1\n"
  perl:  a = Xa1|Xa2|   b = Xb1|   c = Yc1|   (nothing on STDOUT but "done")
  pcl:   a = Xa1|       b = Xb1|   c = Yc1|   and "Xa2" goes to STDOUT
So after the inner loop (with its own `local *ARGVOUT`) ends, the OUTER loop's output handle is not
re-selected: the restored ARGVOUT glob is not the selected handle any more.  perl keeps the in-place
state as magic in *ARGVOUT{IO} and re-selects it when the local glob is restored.  io/nargv.t also has
"check setuid mode preserved" (row 6), already failing.
subject: Nested in-place edit: after an inner `while (<>)` with its own `local *ARGV; local *ARGVOUT` returns, the outer $^I loop's prints go to STDOUT instead of the outer file (io/nargv.t 11/2 -> 5/1 now that `local $^I` takes effect)
